question: How can an expensive measurement be studied in a large cohort without measuring everyone?

kulathinal2007.cite: Kulathinal, Karvanen, Saarela & Kuulasmaa (2007). Case-cohort design in practice – experiences from the MORGAM Project. Epidemiologic Perspectives & Innovations 4: 15.
kulathinal2007.checked: every quote read word for word in the Europe PMC full text (PMC2216006) on 20 Nov 2026; places are its numbered sections, whose titles were read in the same XML; in-text reference numbers are left out

steps.title: Start with a cohort
steps.text: Take a large cohort that is followed up and has stored samples, where measuring everyone (a genotype, a biomarker) would cost too much.

quotes.text: Cohort sampling designs are used in follow-up studies when large cohorts are needed to observe enough cases but it is not feasible to collect data on all covariates for the whole cohort.

steps.title: Random subcohort
steps.text: Draw a random sample of the whole cohort, without looking at who later becomes a case.

quotes.text: a random subsample of the original cohort (subcohort), selected independently of the definition of cases

steps.title: Add every case
steps.text: Add every person who develops the outcome during follow-up. Measure the costly exposure only in this case-cohort set.

quotes.text: all cases outside the subcohort, i.e. all members of the cohort developing any or all events of interest during the follow-up. The union of (1) and (2) is referred to as the case-cohort set.
Commonly used designs such as the case-control or the nested case-control design require genotyping of all the cases and matched controls for each case.

steps.title: Reuse for outcomes
steps.text: Because the subcohort was drawn at random, the same subcohort serves as comparison for several outcomes, and describes the whole cohort.

quotes.text: a distinct advantage of the case-cohort design is that the selected subcohort can be used for analysing several endpoints of interest.

steps.title: Weight the analysis
steps.text: Cases are over-represented, so the analysis weights people back to the whole cohort, for example by the inverse of the subcohort sampling fraction.

quotes.text: Adjustments to the partial likelihood are required because the cases are overrepresented in the case-cohort set and therefore unadjusted risk sets in the partial likelihood would not represent the original study cohort.
Here the subcohort members are weighted by the inverse of the sampling fraction at the event time
quotes.where: section 6.2, Analysis of time-to-event data (Barlow's weighting)

limits: Prentice (1986), the card's reference, was not read in this task; the steps follow Kulathinal et al. (2007), who cite it as the design's theoretical foundation.
The EPIC-InterAct numbers on the card were not checked in this task.
The nested case–control variant is mentioned only as a contrast; its own analysis (matched risk sets) is not shown.
No threat quotes: neither of the card's threats (measurement error, selection bias) is defined in the source read.
